review.review: The Mage defeated Goo, then starved to death after entrance-shop scouting exhausted its budget. The terminal public message explicitly confirms starvation (decision 3351, accepted transition line 9720; terminal observation line 9723), rather than a skeleton kill. An earlier initiating defect is visible at decisions 2054–2056: scouting reaches cell 931 (lines 5968–5969), loot preparation immediately sends the hero back toward 892 (lines 5970–5971), and shop scouting selects 931 again (lines 5973–5974). This repeats through decision 2064. The selecting source only marks the current scouting position exhausted inside peaceful preparation; an earlier preparation selection bypasses that bookkeeping. The shop then keeps treating an already reached frontier as untried. The shop-budget failure appears at decision 2180, line 6252, followed by advancing fallback waits. The proposed correction records a visibly observed arrival following the specific shop-scouting step during observation update, before another controller can preempt peaceful preparation. It changes neither the search budget nor shop-visitation, loot, hazard, or mandatory progression requirements. A condensed deterministic fixture fails on original policy source and passes with the correction; all 1601 Python tests pass, with four skips. No original runtime memory was reconstructed and no replacement decision on the actual run is certified. This establishes the receipt defect and its narrow repair, not that this change would find the shop or prevent starvation.
review.learnings: Remember visibly reached entrance-scouting positions even when loot or safety interrupts the next preparation step. Keep scouting receipts separate from actual shop visitation and collection, and retain all mandatory progression pickups. Removing this repeated approach does not establish shop discovery or survival.
